commands.openPair: Open pair: attachment in the main area, note pinned right
commands.backfill: Create missing notes for all groups

notices.noGroup: "${file}" does not belong to any mapping group.
notices.noteBlocked: A different note already occupies that path for "${file}".
notices.renameNeedsBoth: Enter both the old and the new property name.

refresh.title: Refresh metadata
refresh.subtitle: Pick one side per property for "${note}". Unselected rows stay as they are.
refresh.noChanges: The extracted metadata matches the note. Nothing to choose.

groups.heading: Mapping groups
groups.desc: Each group maps one attachment folder to one note folder, with its own extensions, naming and field table. The most specific attachment folder wins when groups are nested.
groups.empty: No groups yet. Add one to start mapping attachments to notes.

fieldSources.vault: From the vault and the file itself

fields.desc: Toggle what gets written, and rename any property to match your vault's conventions. Two fields may share a property name — the first non-empty one wins.

group.removeConfirm: Delete the group "${name}"? Notes already created stay where they are.

attachmentsFolder.name: Attachments folder
attachmentsFolder.desc: Files placed here get a note.

notesFolder.name: Notes folder
notesFolder.desc: Where the notes are created. May sit above the attachments folder.

mirror.name: Mirror subfolders
mirror.desc: Recreate the attachment's subfolder tree under the notes folder.

extensions.name: Watched extensions
extensions.desc: Comma separated, e.g. .pdf, .epub. Only these files are picked up.

noteName.name: Note name
noteName.desc: Variables: {{basename}} (no extension), {{name}} (with extension), {{ext}}. If the name is taken by another attachment, the extension is added back.

linkTemplate.name: Link format
linkTemplate.desc: Value written into the link field, e.g. [[{{basename}}]] or [[{{path}}]]. Use the full path if two attachments share a name.

embed.name: Embed the attachment
embed.desc: Write an embed of the attachment into the note body.

heading.name: Write an H1 heading
heading.desc: Off by default so the note title is not repeated inside the note.

autoCreate.name: Create a note when an attachment is added

autoDelete.name: Delete the note when the attachment is deleted
autoDelete.desc: The note goes to the same trash as the attachment.

syncUpdated.name: Keep the updated field in sync
syncUpdated.desc: Rewrites the updated property whenever the attachment changes on disk.

pdfExtraction.name: Read PDF metadata
pdfExtraction.desc: Title, author, subject, keywords, dates, producer and page count.

doiLookup.name: Look up DOI / ISBN online
doiLookup.desc: Finds an identifier in the PDF metadata (and, if Obsidian's PDF engine is reachable, on the first pages), then queries CrossRef or Open Library.

sanitize.name: Sanitize list values
sanitize.desc: Strip characters Obsidian rejects in tags from list fields such as keywords.

baseFile.name: Generate a base file
baseFile.desc: Creates a .base index whose columns follow the enabled fields. Existing base files are never overwritten.

baseFolder.name: Base file folder
baseFolder.desc: Leave empty to keep it in the notes folder.

backfill.name: Create missing notes
backfill.desc: Scan this group's attachments and create the notes that do not exist yet.

renameProperty.name: Rename a property in existing notes
renameProperty.desc: Renaming a property above only affects new writes. This rewrites notes already in this group.

link.name: Attachment link
link.desc: Link to the attachment, built from the link format above.

path.name: File path
path.desc: Full vault path. Also used to prove which attachment a note belongs to.

pdfTitle.name: Title
pdfTitle.desc: PDF title, falling back to the file name.

pdfKeywords.name: Keywords
pdfKeywords.desc: PDF keywords, written as a list.

pdfCreated.name: PDF created
pdfCreated.desc: Creation date recorded inside the PDF.

pdfModified.name: PDF modified
pdfModified.desc: Modification date recorded inside the PDF.

pdfCreator.name: PDF creator
pdfCreator.desc: Application that produced the original document.

lookupTitle.name: Title (online)
lookupTitle.desc: Title from CrossRef or Open Library. Shares the title property by default.

lookupAuthor.name: Author (online)
lookupAuthor.desc: Authors from CrossRef or Open Library.

lookupYear.name: Year
lookupYear.desc: Publication year from the online lookup.
